- Model consistently underestimates prices in early forecast windows, especially after sharp declines or volatility spikes; adjust downward bias by 2–5% for first 5–7 days.
- Overshoots after price spikes (e.g., 35+), particularly in mid-to-late forecast horizon (days 10–20), suggesting overconfidence in momentum; cap forecast peaks at +3–5% above recent high.
- Mean reversion bias: model fails to recognize price pullback after 30–40%+ spikes; apply 1–2% downward correction in 10–15 day window if sentiment remains flat or negative.
- Sentiment history is uniformly zero across all examples — no behavioral signal — so ignore sentiment-based adjustments unless sentiment shifts >0.3 in magnitude.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts often overestimate mid-term volatility; reduce forecast variance by 15–20% for days 15–25 to align with observed smoothing.
- No correction needed for early days (1–5) if no recent spike; model is generally accurate in stable periods.
- If true outcome shows sudden reversal (e.g., 35→32→36), model tends to lag by 2–3 days; add 1–2 day lag correction for price reversal events.
